hints: Remember there are two separate tests here, shifting the position to the right and actually changing the value of Kc.
Notice that $\Delta H = +77.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so the forward reaction to make $\text{NO}$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ is endothermic and takes in heat.
Think about which single condition both favours the endothermic direction and is the only factor that can change Kc.
walkthrough:
**Separate position from Kc**

Think like a teacher with two checklists. Position of equilibrium can be moved by concentration, pressure and temperature. But the value of Kc is only changed by temperature.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{only a change in temperature changes } K_c$$

**Check what pressure does**

Count the gas moles. Left has 2 mol of $\text{NOCl}$, right has 2 + 1 = 3 mol.

$$2\text{NOCl(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$$
A decrease in pressure favours the side with more moles, so it does shift right. But it leaves Kc exactly the same, so it fails the second test.

**Check what temperature does**

The forward reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H$ positive). Adding heat by increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb that heat.
That means equilibrium moves to the right, more $\text{NO}$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ are made, and Kc gets larger. That passes both tests, so this is the answer.

options.A: A decrease in pressure does shift equilibrium to the right because the right side has 3 gas moles versus 2 on the left. However, pressure changes do not change Kc, only temperature does, so it fails the second condition.
options.B: A decrease in temperature removes heat and favours the exothermic direction, which is the reverse reaction here. This shifts equilibrium to the left and decreases Kc, the opposite of what is wanted.
options.C: An increase in pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles, which is the left side with 2 mol of NOCl. This shifts equilibrium to the left and also leaves Kc unchanged.
options.D: An increase in temperature adds heat and favours the endothermic forward reaction ($\Delta H$ positive). This moves equilibrium to the right to make more NO and Cl2, and because temperature is the only factor that changes Kc, the value of Kc increases.
